feed.title: Truth Social is selling faster access to Trump posts. Is that legal?
feed.summary: Trump Media's new "Truth API" service offers paying clients expedited access to former President Trump's social media posts, including official announcements that could move markets, raising significant legal and ethical concerns. Critics argue this practice gives preferential access to critical government information, potentially violating the First and Fifth Amendments, and differs from other news services because the information originates directly from a former president who stands to profit. A federal lawsuit has been filed, and congressional Democrats are proposing legislation to block such pay-for-access schemes for government employees' communications.

feed.title: NorthStrive Biosciences Announces The Filing of Two U.S. Patent Applications Targeting Microgravity-Induced Muscle Loss During Long-Duration Spaceflight
feed.summary: NorthStrive Biosciences, a subsidiary of PMGC Holdings Inc., has filed two U.S. patent applications for its lead assets, EL-22 and EL-32, to address microgravity-induced muscle loss during long-duration spaceflight. These filings aim to position EL-22 and EL-32 as muscle-preservation platforms for both terrestrial markets and the emerging medical needs of human space exploration. The company emphasizes that these preclinical candidates are not yet approved by any regulatory authority and are not currently part of any agreements with space agencies.

feed.title: NorthStrive says no drug is approved for spaceflight muscle loss; it files two applications
feed.summary: NorthStrive Biosciences, a subsidiary of PMGC Holdings (Nasdaq: ELAB), announced the filing of two U.S. patent applications for its preclinical candidates EL-22 and EL-32, aiming to preserve lean muscle mass in humans exposed to microgravity. These filings extend NorthStrive's intellectual property strategy from GLP-1/obesity-related muscle loss and animal health into spaceflight-associated muscle atrophy, leveraging the same myostatin and activin A targeting biology. The company states that no pharmacologic therapy is currently approved for microgravity-induced muscle loss and emphasizes that these candidates are preclinical, not yet evaluated in humans for this specific indication, and there are no existing agreements with space agencies.
